title: HandMimicX: Learning Human-Like Dexterous Manipulation via an Object-Centric Policy from Egocentric Videos
abstract: Learning dexterous manipulation from human videos remains an open challenge, particularly in the context of transferring a single demonstration into a spatially generalizable robotic skill and maintaining physically plausible human-like interactions. Unlike prior works that emphasize hand-motion imitation, we introduce an object-centric framework for acquiring dexterous skills from egocentric human RGB-D videos. Within our framework, we formulate the reinforcement learning (RL) objective in terms of object motion to decouple the underlying skill from the specific hand trajectory and impose constraints on hand-object interaction states to promote more anatomically natural hand configurations. Extensive experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate that our method enables efficient learning from human videos and generalizable skill transfer across novel spatial configurations.

Ho 5 Zipeng Ye3,† Peng Jiao 1,2 Haoqian Wang1,† 1Tsinghua University 2TsingTec 3MeiTuan 4The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen 5NVIDIA Fig. 1:HandMimicX: We present an object-centric framework for learning dexterous manipulation skills from a single egocentric demonstration, leveraging simulation-based reinforcement learning and sim-to-real policy transfer. The framework consists of three stages. First, we reconstruct the demonstrated hand–object interaction from the input video, recovering the hand–object motion trajectory, object geometry, and task-relevant interaction priors. Second, using the reconstructed object mesh and interaction priors, we train an object-centric tracking policy to manipulate the object to spatially randomized target object poses, denoted asRT n. By optimizing the policy across diverse target poses, the robot acquires spatial generalization beyond the original human demonstration. Finally, the learned policy is transferred to the real robot and executed using observations from an RGB-D camera, enabling dexterous manipulation in the real-world environment.
